independent_algebra_check.checked: Signs and coefficients in the supplied formula agree. d-1 and d-3 denote real arithmetic after casting the dimension; natural truncated subtraction must not silently replace them.
independent_algebra_check.dimension_edge_cases: The exact identity needs no d>=3. d=0 is vacuous for supplied sphere-valued processes on a probability space; d=1 must remain covered. The sign simplification for d>=3 is a separate consequence.
independent_algebra_check.moment_scope: Taking expectations retains E[r^2], the fourth moment. Neither equality with the square of E[r] nor independence across particles is used.

conclusions: D(b)-D(a)=integral_a^b G(s) ds for 0<=a<=b, using the oriented real interval integral.
D is absolutely continuous on each [0,T] with finite T>=0.
The ordinary derivative equals G at every strictly positive time.
At zero the derivative is only relative to [0,infinity), equal to G(0).
not_allowed_as_added_inputs: Derivative-martingale construction or its zero expectation.
Separate whole-path continuity or initial measurability.
Global drift bounds, extra Lipschitz constants, or supplied noise L2/drift L1 certificates.
Independence among different particle Brownian motions.
objects: Finite particle set Fin N with N>0 and ambient Euclidean space R^d for arbitrary d:N.
The literal norm-one sphere S and paired configuration space S^N x S^N.
One probability measure and one complete right-continuous filtration.
For each particle i a standard R^d-valued Brownian motion relative to that filtration; both components of pair i use its same literal coordinate drivers.
Supplied sphere-valued jointly measurable strongly progressive X_i and Y_i.
A fixed real lambda>=0 and two jointly continuous non-radial drift fields on nonnegative time and paired configurations.
D is the finite average of expected squared ambient chord lengths, R4 the corresponding average of fourth moments, and L twice the averaged learning-drift pairing.
inventory.quantifier_and_event_scope: For every positive finite horizon H, one probability-one event supports all its times and all finite particle/coordinate equations simultaneously. The source does not impose independence between particle drivers. Conclusions are pointwise deterministic expectation identities; no samplewise nonlinear balance is assumed.
inventory.real_time_extension: Processes and coefficients live at nonnegative times. The real-time observables evaluate them at max(t,0); the source does not assert a two-sided derivative at zero.
standing_assumptions: Probability measure and usual filtration; each B_i is standard relative to the entire common past filtration.
Joint measurability and strong progressivity of the supplied processes.
Fixed nonnegative lambda, including zero; joint continuity of both learning drift fields.
The actual original coordinate integral SDEs, with common pairwise Brownian coordinates, on horizon-wise simultaneous full-measure events.

necessary_for_stated_route: Same driver within each pair for the displayed diffusion cross term.
Fixed nonnegative lambda for the real square-root diffusion coefficient and continuous-generator conclusion.
Continuous drifts and simultaneous-on-horizon coordinate equations for the requested pointwise time regularity.
not_necessary_for_this_identity: A supplied tangent-drift assumption once actual solutions are already sphere valued

phase: Natural-source-only analysis before opening candidate signature, binder seal, source inventory, reuse plan or implementation.

proof_nodes.bridge_to_verify: Existing constructors must accept the actual common drivers and exact coefficient representatives without requesting path continuity or an already-proved quadratic balance.
proof_nodes.operation: Build finite-horizon coefficients from the original SDE data.
produces: Finite-horizon deterministic drift bounds, progressive/measurable drift and diffusion coefficients.
Drift L1 and projected-noise L2 admissibility; measurable initial coordinates.
requires: Progressive processes and coordinate projection formulas.

proof_nodes.bridge_to_verify: Intersect finitely many coordinate/particle events and, if needed, countably many integer-horizon events. Pointwise-in-time a.e. equalities alone would not suffice.
proof_nodes.operation: Recover continuous whole paths from the coordinate SDE.
produces: A common full-measure event of continuous paired paths on each finite horizon.
requires: Continuous versions of completed Ito integrals and indefinite integrals of the drift.

proof_nodes.bridge_to_verify: The pair must be a single driven state with shared noise columns. Replacing it by unrelated component noises loses the required cross-variation.
proof_nodes.operation: Apply an existing compact-state Ito formula to each paired state and the quadratic observable.
produces: Actual quadratic-observable Ito balance and its derivative stochastic integral.
requires: A Euclidean paired-state encoding with compact range S x S.
The same Brownian-coordinate family for both blocks of each particle.

proof_nodes.bridge_to_verify: The diffusion term is 2 lambda sum_j||(P_X-P_Y)e_j||^2. Dimension offsets are real, and the negative quartic remains inside expectation.
requires: Unit norms and the projection algebra above.

proof_nodes.bridge_to_verify: Mean zero and Fubini/integrability must be consequences of the existing theorem and bounded coefficients, not new source assumptions. No inter-particle cross terms occur in this observable.
proof_nodes.operation: Center the actual stochastic term, take expectations and average finitely.
produces: The deterministic two-time signed balance for D with generator G.
requires: Derivative-noise L2 integrability on the compact range.
The completed Ito process starts at zero and is a true centered martingale.

proof_nodes.bridge_to_verify: Use deterministic FTC after proving expectation continuity. A merely measurable-temperature theorem alone supplies only a.e. derivatives and needs this additional continuity upgrade.
proof_nodes.operation: Upgrade the expectation balance using continuity of G.
produces: Continuity of G at every nonnegative time.
Finite-interval absolute continuity of D, derivatives at every positive time, and the right derivative at zero.
requires: Compact domination on each finite time interval.
Fixed lambda and continuous drift fields.
